summary: Planning-only phase (no implementation). Re-derived all four outstanding production defects directly from current production source, not from historical summary prose: B1 (ValidatedAuthorityProjection._validator_seal, runtime_authority.py:774, is identity-only and copyable via dataclasses.replace()); B7 (RuntimeDispatchIdentity built by _identity_registration_digest, runtime_dispatch_permission.py:249, without re-checking the durable RuntimeDispatchIdentityTracker registry at request-build time); N1 (validate_approval, runtime_authority.py:820, accepts approval objects without canonical-store lookup-by-ID against RuntimeInvocationApprovalStore); N2 (ApprovalProvenance.approver_id, runtime_authority.py:291-292, is an unauthenticated caller-supplied string). Confirmed AuthenticatedHumanPrincipal (hpac_verifier.py) still has zero production consumers (grep -rn 'hpac_verifier\|AuthenticatedHumanPrincipal' src/pcae --include=*.py outside tests/hpac_verifier.py itself returns only a docstring-only mention in human_authenticator.py:120). Selected Option A staging architecture (structural repair of all four defects now, gated by a deterministic-NON-REAL hard-rejection point placed at approval canonicalization in runtime_authority.py, since verify_human_authentication remains permanently NON-REAL until real FIDO2 exists) over Option B (defer all positive authority projection) and Option C (split further) -- justified because B1/B7/N1/N2 are provenance/revalidation defects, not premature-positive-authority defects, and are fully closeable under a fail-closed NON-REAL gate. Adjudicated F1 (CLOSED, prerequisite satisfied), F2 (HPAC-REQ-054 Step 4 independent challenge-digest recomputation -- reclassified from non-blocking to a required prerequisite inside the next implementation phase, since production consumption is exactly the context F2 was previously deferred pending), F3/F4 (remain non-blocking, deferred, documentation/naming debt only), F7 (remains non-blocking; production integration does not change the same-process code-execution risk, which the repair does not attempt to solve). Recorded an explicit contradiction/correction (Sec 11.1 of the canonical doc): the .1R.2 sub-phase's original STOP on N2 (RIHAC-001 v1.0, no authentication mechanism existed) was resolved by the .1R.3-.1R.5.2.1 contract-evolution chain (RIHAC-001 v2.0, HPAC-001 v2.0) but this lift was never previously stated explicitly in any phase doc -- this planning document states it explicitly, without modifying any contract text. Verified (not merely asserted) that B1/B7/N1/N2 plumbing can be safely built before real FIDO2 and before the real protected UI, provided the NON-REAL hard-rejection point is in place first. Planned forward (not implemented) Gate 5 and Gate 9 responsibilities per RDGO-001 v3.0; confirmed no Gate 5 implementation exists anywhere in source (only docstring forward-references in hpac_verifier.py) and that Gate 9 has only an inert model/store (runtime_invocation_authority_consumption.py, explicitly documented in its own docstring as having no gate wiring, no gate-9 caller, and no real-approval consumption). Located POL-005 as the ExecutionDisabledRule in permission_broker_foundation.py:446-475, confirmed unaffected. Produced a production file matrix, a B1/B7/N1/N2 traceability matrix, and a 21-case defensive validation matrix for the next implementation phase. Selected one-phase packaging for the B1/B7/N1/N2 implementation repair (not split further) because all four defects share one trust boundary in two production modules, deferring Gate 5/Gate 9 coordinator wiring as a separate, later, unscheduled chapter (no phase ID invented for it, consistent with this project's no-invent-an-ID discipline). Froze next phase IDs: 149O.20L.7O.3W.1R.2B.1R.1.1R.7 (B1/B7/N1/N2 production authority repair implementation) and 149O.20L.7O.3W.1R.2B.1R.1.1R.8 (its independent verification). No production trust-path file modified this phase (planning-only: runtime_authority.py, runtime_dispatch_permission.py, runtime_invocation_approval_store.py, runtime_invocation_authority_consumption.py, hpac_verifier.py, permission_broker_foundation.py all untouched, independently confirmed by git diff/git log). No contract modified. No Permission Broker integration. No runtime enablement. No real FIDO2 or protected UI work. Requires separate explicit human authorization to begin .1R.7.
